why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` IS an `rclcpp::Node`, so this is `rclcpp::Node::create_callback_group`, inherited, with `cpp:Node::create_callback_group`'s contract. The extractor records only the members a class declares, so this key correlates as upstream-only even though the name resolves.

Before phase-482 W4: `nros::Node` has callback groups (RFC-0002 maps them onto RTOS priority tiers). Reached through `nros::Node`, which has it. our `nros::LifecycleNode` is a MIXIN over an executor handle, not a `Node` subclass: RFC-0002 puts one executor per RTOS task and the lifecycle state machine lives on the EXECUTOR (that is what `rclc_executor_lifecycle_*` and `register_lifecycle_services` drive), while the node-side API stays on `nros::Node`. rclcpp's `LifecycleNode` re-declares the whole `Node` surface because it cannot inherit from `Node`; ours does not need to, and duplicating ~50 methods onto a second class would cost image size for nothing. What a ported node loses: it holds a `Node&` and a `LifecycleNode` instead of one object.
